summary: Priority orders assignment preference but is subordinate to all hard constraints.
rule: When not all demand can be served, higher-priority jobs are preferred for assignment, but priority cannot override capacity, time windows, skills, precedence, max-stops, or max-duration. Outsourcing_cost (the cost of leaving a task unassigned) acts as a priority override — when set, tasks with higher outsourcing cost are assigned first. An unsatisfiable high-priority task still goes to result.unassigned.
testingGuidance: Combination: tight capacity + one high-priority + one low-priority job competing for the last slot -> high-priority assigned, low-priority unassigned.
Combination: high-priority job whose only skill is unavailable on any vehicle -> still unassigned despite priority.
Interaction: two jobs with equal priority; one has outsourcing_cost 100, other 50 -> cost-based job assigned first.
